name: scene-feedback-harness
description: Review reference images and reconstructed scenes, annotate visual errors, and deliver image feedback through MCP tools and events.

defaultPrompt: 进入人工调试模式，让我在参考图和当前场景上指出问题。
Review this reconstruction with annotated visual feedback.
interface.longDescription: Compare reference images with reconstructed 3D scenes, mark visual errors, and share original and annotated evidence through a project-specific MCP service. Type @ in one prompt to reference the currently selected object or part and this round’s unsent annotations. The native prompt input and chat history display icons with stable numbers: object 🧊1, part 🧩1, mark 📍1, image 🖼️1, human evidence 🧍1, correction ✏️1 and time 🕒1. Rounded source cards provide full source previews, full names, exact source details and removal. Each kind has independent numbering, repeated sources reuse their number, and existing drafts migrate automatically while preserving exact source bindings. Archived data retains protocol tokens and precise source metadata. Double-click an item or part in live 3D, an object-list row or the selected name to insert its exact reference. Single clicks still select; orbiting and dragging do not cite. Press F to focus the selected target. Double-click the progress thumb, reference frame counter or a saved screenshot time to cite that precise source. Pending thumb citations wait for their target frame and are canceled by a subsequent seek or source change. Type / to cite exact moments or spans from the current clip and this round’s evidence, or double-click the current timeline time to cite the actual clock; Enter or Space also works when the time has keyboard focus. The prompt uses short time references such as 🕒1; clickable cards show precise times, views and reference frames, and sending restores the complete exact description. Repeating the same source and moment reuses its number, while different times stay separate and draft reloads preserve bindings. Editing times are expressed in the prompt. Drag images or use evidence buttons to add other visual references. The scene view keeps one row of compact cards below the image: interactive 3D first, followed by frozen screenshots in capture order. Cards smoothly expand in place on mouse hover or visible keyboard focus; touchscreens keep compact cards for direct taps. Annotation tools appear in a horizontal toolbar when the upper area of the reference or scene pane is hovered or tapped on a touchscreen, or the image has visible keyboard focus; tools compact or wrap to fit the pane width. Moving into the tools or More menu keeps them open; leaving the upper area and tools closes them after a short delay while preserving the selected tool and ongoing gestures. Switch camera views with reference thumbnails while keeping the current clip time. The glass conversation panel starts at 480px wide on desktop and expands to 760px on hover, keyboard focus or touch tap, enlarging only the input area and existing evidence. History opens manually and stays closed after the panel automatically shrinks and expands again. Evidence and details fold temporarily while saved size, position and drafts remain intact. After the pointer leaves and typing stops, it shrinks and closes mention, time and attachment menus; lingering focus, completed selections and idle menus do not hold it open. Active typing including IME composition, keyboard navigation, touch editing, dragging and pending answers keep it expanded, while input, references and Send remain available. It can be moved by dragging its header background, with per-session position preferences, viewport fitting and a reset gesture. Overlay opacity and ground direction are directly available in the scene toolbar; reference camera alignment sits between the two views in comparison mode and above the scene in immersive mode. Drawing on live 3D automatically freezes the current view and completes the same gesture on its screenshot. Further marks stay on that image; returning to 3D and drawing again creates another screenshot while retaining earlier evidence. The workbench supports multiple camera views, dynamic frames, imported WholeBody133 evidence and manual hand keypoint corrections. Human reconstruction and tracking run in a separate capsule skill. Feedback delivery selects relevant cited and marked sources and needed current views, omits empty annotation copies and identical images, and keeps complete evidence archived. MCP feedback returns compact summaries by default; workspace_get_feedback can return full archived fields on request. Experimental MCP Events delivery requires a supporting host and a verified subscription.
